text:
nina: hey all, jumping in on day 2 — blocked from several private repos. browser shows a 403 and says "You must enable two-factor authentication" even though i turned it on last night. accepted the invite with nina.work@redwood.com but my GH primary is nina.personal@gmail.com.
oliver: welcome! quick Q: are you cloning over HTTPS or SSH? and did you set up a PAT or SSH key?
nina: was trying HTTPS first. created a PAT earlier this morning before joining the org.
it-admin: note: GitHub requires SAML/SSO to authorize PATs for org repos. If you created the PAT before authorizing SSO it won't work for org-scoped access. Try authorizing SSO via your profile -> Organizations -> Redwood Inference.
nina: i toggled SSO/authorize and re-created a PAT, but still getting credential prompts. `git push` returns `remote: Permission to redwood/private-sdk.git denied to ninapersonal.`
security-bot: SCIM event: user nina.work@redwood.com provisioned -> teams: sdk, integrations (2026-01-15T12:45:10Z).
jordan: i bet your git credential helper is caching the old PAT tied to the personal account. run `git credential-osxkeychain erase` (mac) or on Linux clear `~/.git-credentials`, or run `gh auth login --web` to refresh credentials.
nina: ran `gh auth status` -> shows logged in as nina.personal@gmail.com (ugh). did `gh auth logout` then `gh auth login --web` and explicitly picked nina.work@redwood.com this time.
oliver: good — also check `ssh -T git@github.com` to see which user your SSH key maps to. if the output is your personal handle you'll need to add your work SSH key and/or remove any old keys from agent.
nina: `ssh -T git@github.com` -> `Hi ninapersonal! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.` so SSH is still personal. i have one key in `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` that i added before onboarding.
it-admin: two options: 1) generate a new key for work and add it to your GitHub account (preferred), or 2) add a host alias in `~/.ssh/config` and point the repo to that host. Also check that your key wasn't accidentally added as a deploy key on another repo — that would make GitHub treat it as repo-scoped.
jordan: i checked org deploy-keys quickly — your key fingerprint shows up as a deploy key on docs.redwood (read-only). that's probably why SSH auth didn't give you user-level perms. we can reassign it to your user account.
nina: created `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood`, added the pub key to my GH account, `ssh -T git@github.com` now -> `Hi ninawork! You've successfully authenticated...`
security-bot: Reminder: make sure 2FA is enabled on your primary work account; org policy enforces it.
nina: switched remote to SSH and tried a push -> `remote: Repository not found.` still blocked for a couple repos even though others work.
itol-admin: sometimes SCIM/team sync hasn't applied fine-grained repo grants yet. i've triggered a reprovision for nina.work@redwood.com; can you refresh the repo page and try again in ~2 minutes?
olo: reprovision done. please try now.
nina: tried again after a few minutes — push succeeded for sdk and integrations repos but still 403 on `private-sdk-cli` which is under a different team. on the repo page it says "You are not a member of any teams with access to this repository."
jordan: i added you to `cli-team` manually; you should get an email. also double-check the repo has branch protection rules that forbid force-pushes — that would surface as permission denied for that action only.
nina: got the team invite and accepted, clones/pushes now work everywhere. huge thanks. :tada:
oliver: nice troubleshooting flow — follow-ups: 1) we'll update the welcome doc to emphasize authorizing SSO before creating PATs, 2) avoid reusing a single SSH key as both deploy key and user key, 3) ops will confirm SCIM timing in first-hour provisioning.
it-admin: created ticket ONB-2026 to add SSO/PAT/SSH troubleshooting to the new-hire checklist and to audit recently added deploy keys for conflicts. welcome aboard, @nina :wave:
